Regularized Portfolio Optimization Engine: 1/N vs. Markowitz

Historical (academic industry portfolios) | Ken French 30 industry portfolios (value-weighted, daily) | final 2015-01-01 to 2025-12-31 | cost 10 bps/$ | monthly signal, next-close execution | run 20261123T233332Z_default_a2d5acfe

Findings from saved results

  • Final 2015-2025: net Sharpe EQW 0.55, SAMPLE_MV 0.66, COST_AWARE_REG_MV 0.63. 5 of 5 bootstrap intervals for the Sharpe difference vs 1/N include zero (COST_AWARE_REG_MV [-0.15, +0.30], SAMPLE_MV [-0.13, +0.31]), so these differences are not resolved.
  • The cost penalty cut recurring half-gross turnover from 1.92x to 0.88x per year relative to identical forecasts without it (fees 8.3% vs 3.8% of starting split NAV); net Sharpe 0.65 vs 0.63.
  • The point advantage depends on the lookback: SAMPLE_MV net Sharpe by window 126d 0.63, 252d 0.66, 504d 0.55 vs EQW 0.55 (prespecified one-at-a-time sweep, same split).
  • Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage was light (mean alpha 0.033) yet cut the median condition number by 37% (335 to 213); targets moved little (mean L1 distance 0.009 vs SAMPLE_MV), while mean shrinkage moved them far more (0.405).

Assets: Assets are the 30 Kenneth French value-weighted industry research portfolios (returns include distributions), not individual stocks or directly tradable ETFs. Costs are stylized reallocation costs between research portfolios, not execution-cost estimates. Weights and notional reallocations are hypothetical.
